Kǒngzǐ, in his first official position,
was made magistrate of Zhōngdū.
He established regulations for supporting the living and burying the dead.
The old and young ate differently,
the strong and weak had different duties,
men and women walked on separate paths;
lost items were not picked up on the road,
utensils were not carved with false decorations;
coffins were made of four cùn wood,
outer coffins of five cùn wood,
tombs followed the shape of hills,
without mounds or trees.
After a year of implementing these,
the feudal lords of the west imitated them.
Duke Dìng said to Kǒngzǐ,
"If your method is learned,
what will become of the state of Lǔ?"
Kǒngzǐ replied,
"Even the whole world would be manageable!
Why only the state of Lǔ?"
Therefore, after two years,
Duke Dìng appointed him Minister of Works.
Thereupon, he distinguished the natures of the five types of soil,
so that things each obtained the appropriate place for their growth,
and all found their proper place.
Previously,
the Jì family buried Duke Zhāo south of the tomb path;
Kǒngzǐ dug a ditch and connected all the tombs,
saying to Jì Huánzǐ,
"You are belittling the ruler to publicize your own offense.
fēi lǐ yě. is not proper etiquette.
Jīn hé zhī, Now connecting them,
suǒ yǐ yǎn fūzǐ zhī bù chén." is in order to conceal the fact that the masters are not loyal subjects."
Yóu sīkōng wèi Lǔ dà sī kòu, He served as Minister of Works, then as Grand Minister of Justice for Lǔ,
shè fǎ ér bù yòng, established laws which were not even needed,
wú jiān mín. and there were no deceitful people.
Dìng Gōng yǔ Qí hóu huì yú Jiágǔ. Duke Dìng met with the Marquis of Qí at Jiágǔ.
Kǒngzǐ shè xiàng shì, Kǒngzǐ acted as the master of ceremonies,

yǒu wǔ shì zhě bì yǒu wén bèi. and those engaged in military affairs must have civil preparations.
Gǔ zhě zhū hóu bìng chū jiāng, In ancient times when feudal lords went beyond their borders together,
bì jù guān yǐ cóng, they would certainly bring a full complement of officials with them,
qǐng jù zuǒ yòu sīmǎ." I request to bring the left and right commanders."
Dìng Gōng cóng zhī. Duke Dìng followed his advice.
Zhì huì suǒ, Arriving at the meeting place,
wèi tán, they built an altar
tǔ jiē sān děng, with three levels of earthen steps,
yǐ yù lǐ xiāng jiàn, in order to meet each other with proper ceremony,
yī ràng ér dēng. bowing and yielding as they ascended.
After the presentation of ceremonial wine was complete,
the envoy from Qí 齊, a man from Lái 萊, used soldiers and drums to create a disturbance,
threatening Dìng Gōng 定公.
Kǒngzǐ 孔子 went up the steps and advanced,
urging the duke to withdraw.
He said:
"Gentlemen,
they are using weapons against him.
Our two lords are seeking amity,
these captives from distant barbarian tribes,
dare to disrupt it with weapons;
this is not how the lord of Qí 齊 commands the feudal lords.
Barbarians do not plot against the civilized,
foreigners do not disturb the Chinese,
captives do not interfere with covenants,
weapons do not coerce friendship.
To the spirits, it is inauspicious;
to virtue, it is a transgression of righteousness;
to people, it is a loss of propriety.
Your lord must not allow this."
The lord of Qí 齊 felt ashamed in his heart,
and waved them away to avoid the situation.
After a while,
Qí 齊 began to perform palace music,
and actors and dwarfs performed in front.
Kǒngzǐ 孔子 quickly stepped forward,
ascending the steps,
not completing a single level.
Said:
"A commoner who deceives and insults the feudal lords
deserves to be punished.
I request the Right Sīmǎ to quickly carry out the execution."
Thereupon, he executed the dwarf,
dismembering his body.
The Marquis of Qí was afraid
and appeared ashamed.
As they were about to make an alliance,
the people of Qí added to the written oath, saying:
"If the Qí army goes beyond the border
and does not follow me with three hundred chariots,
may this alliance be like this."
Kǒngzǐ instructed Zī Wúhuán to reply:
"If you do not return the fields of Wènyáng to us,
which we used to fulfill our obligations,
then it will be the same for us."
The Marquis of Qí was about to set up a banquet,
and Kǒngzǐ said to Liángqiū Jù:
"How could you not have heard about the past relations between Qí and Lǔ?
To offer a banquet after the matter is already settled is to trouble the officials.
Furthermore, sacrificial oxen and ivory objects should not leave the temple,
and joyous music should not be performed in the open fields.
To offer a banquet when everything is already prepared
is to abandon propriety.
If it is not fully prepared,
This is using inferior rice.
Using inferior rice is a disgrace to the lord;
Abandoning propriety brings a bad name.
Why don't you consider this?
Now, the offering is a means of displaying virtue.
If it doesn't display virtue,
it's better to have not done it at all."
Consequently, he did not proceed with the offering.
When the Marquis of Qí 齊侯 returned,
he rebuked his ministers, saying:
"Lǔ 魯 uses the way of the superior man to assist its lord,
but you alone use the way of barbarians to instruct me,
causing me to commit offenses."
Thereupon, he returned the four towns he had seized from Lǔ 魯, as well as the fields of Wèn Yáng 汶陽.
Kǒngzǐ 孔子 said to Duke Dìng 定公:
"A household should not store armor,
and a town should not have walls of a hundred *zhì* (3 *zhàng* tall),
according to the ancient regulations.
Now, the Three Families exceed these regulations.
I request that they all be reduced."
Thereupon, he ordered Zhòng Yóu 仲由, the steward of the Jì 季 family, to demolish the three cities.
Shūsūn 叔孫 was displeased with the Jì 季 family.
Because of this, he used Gōngshān Fúráo 公山弗擾, the steward of Fèi 費,
to lead the people of Fèi 費 in an attack on Lǔ 魯.
Kǒngzǐ 孔子, along with Duke Dìng 定公, Jìsūn 季孫, Zhòngsūn 仲孫, and Shūsūn 叔孫,
entered the palace of the Fèi 費 family
Climbing the Terrace of Wǔzǐ.
The people of Fèi attacked it,
reaching the side of the terrace.
Kǒngzǐ ordered Shēn Jūxū and Yuè Qí
to rally the troops,
and descend to attack them.
The people of Fèi were defeated and fled north.
Consequently, he destroyed the walls of the three capitals,
strengthened the ducal house,
weakened the private families,
honored the ruler and humbled the ministers,
and political transformation greatly progressed.
Initially,
in Lǔ, there was a sheep merchant named Shěn Yóushì,
who would regularly give his sheep water in the morning to deceive the market people;
there was a Gōng Shènshì
whose wife was promiscuous and uncontrollable;
there was a Shèn Kuìshì
whose extravagance exceeded the law;
in Lǔ, those who sold livestock
would embellish them to inflate the price.
When Kǒngzǐ took office,
Shěn Yóushì dared not give his sheep water in the morning;
Gōng Shènshì divorced his wife;
Shèn Kuìshì crossed the border and moved away.
After three months,
Then those who sell cattle and horses do not hoard prices;
those who sell piglets do not add adornments;
men and women walking separate their paths;
people do not pick up lost items on the road;
men value loyalty and trustworthiness,
women value chastity and obedience;
visitors from all directions who arrive in the town,
do not seek out the officials,
all feel as if they have returned home.
The Beginning of Execution, Section Two
Kǒngzǐ became the Minister of Justice of Lǔ,
acting as prime minister,
and had a joyous expression.
Zhòng Yóu asked,
"Yóu has heard that the virtuous man does not fear the arrival of misfortune,
and does not rejoice at the arrival of good fortune.
Now, Master, you have gained position and are joyful,
why is this?"
Kǒngzǐ said,
"Indeed!
There is such a saying.
Does it not say to rejoice in valuing those beneath you?"
Thereupon, after governing the court for seven days, he executed the rebellious official Shào Zhèng Mǎo,
executing him beneath the two watchtowers,
displaying his corpse in the court for three days.
Zǐgòng stepped forward and said,
“Now, Shào Zhèng Mǎo was a famous man of Lǔ.
Now that you, Master, are in power and have begun to execute him,
perhaps this is a mistake?”
Confucius said:
“Sit down!
I will tell you the reason for this.
There are five great evils in the world,
and theft is not among them.
The first is being inwardly rebellious and treacherous,
the second is behaving perversely and stubbornly,
the third is speaking falsely and eloquently,
the fourth is remembering shameful things and being knowledgeable,
the fifth is conforming to what is wrong and being ingratiating.
If a person has any one of these five,
then he cannot escape the punishment of a junzi,
zé bùmiǎn jūnzǐ zhī zhū,
and Shào Zhèng Mǎo possesses them all.
His residence is sufficient to gather followers and form a party,
his speeches are sufficient to adorn praises and deceive the masses,
his strength and resistance are sufficient to oppose what is right and stand alone;
this is a treacherous leader of men,
and cannot be eliminated.
Now, Yīn Tāng executed Yǐn Xié,
King Wén executed Pān Zhèng,
Duke Zhōu executed Guǎn Cài,
Grand Duke executed Huá Shì,
Guǎn Zhòng executed Fù Yǐ,
Zǐ Chǎn executed Shǐ Hé,
All these seven men, though living in different eras, were similarly put to death.
It is because these seven men, though living in different eras, shared the same wickedness,
that they could not be pardoned.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
"My heart is heavy with sorrow,
I am angered by the multitude of petty men."
When petty men form a group,
it is indeed a cause for worry."
Kǒngzǐ was the Grand Minister of Justice of Lǔ.
There was a father and son who were in litigation.
The Master had them both arrested and imprisoned together.
For three months, they were not separated.
The father requested that the case be dropped.
The Master then pardoned them.
Jìsūn heard of this
and was displeased.
He said:
"The Minister of Justice is deceiving me!
He previously told me:
'To govern a state, one must first begin with filial piety.'
I intended to execute a filial offender to teach the people about filial piety;
wouldn't that have been a good thing?
But now he has pardoned him.
Why is that?"
Rǎn Yǒu told Kǒngzǐ about this.
Kǒngzǐ sighed deeply and said:
"Wūhū!
For superiors to lose their way and kill their inferiors
is not reasonable.
To not teach them filial piety and then hear their cases
is to kill the innocent.
When the entire army is defeated,
they cannot all be executed.
When the prisons are not well-managed,
punishments cannot be carried out.
Why?
Because the superiors' teachings are not being followed,
the blame does not lie with the people.
To be lenient with orders but strict with punishments
is to be a thief.
To collect taxes without a set time
is to be oppressive.
To declare something a success without trying it out
is to be cruel.
Therefore, if these three are absent,
then punishment can be immediately applied.
The *Shū* [Book of Documents] says:
'Just punishments and just executions,
do not use them to satisfy your own heart,
but only say that there is no matter that has been carefully considered.'
This means one must first teach and then punish.
If one has already presented moral teachings in order to first subdue them,
and they are still not amenable,
then one should promote the worthy to encourage them.
If that is not acceptable,
then abolish it;
if that is still not acceptable,
only then use awe to intimidate them.
If this is done for three years, the people will be upright.
If there are wicked people who do not conform to the transformation,
then deal with them with punishment,
and the people will all know what is a crime.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
‘The Son of Heaven is the support,
causing the people not to be confused.’
Therefore, sternness is present but not tested,
punishments are laid aside and not used.
The present age is not like this;
it disrupts their teachings,
complicates their punishments,
causing the people to be confused and trapped by them,
and then controls them,
therefore, punishments become more numerous and thieves cannot be overcome.
Now, a three-foot barrier,
an empty cart cannot climb it,
why?
Because it is steep;
a hundred-cubit mountain,
a heavy load ascends it,
why?
Because the slope is gradual.
The gradual slope of the present world has been in place for a long time,
Even if there are penal laws,
can the people be prevented from transgressing?"
*Wáng Yán Jiě Dì Sān* (Third Section on Explaining Royal Words)
*Kǒngzǐ* was at leisure,
and *Zēng Shēn* was attending him.
*Kǒngzǐ* said,
"*Shēn*!
The gentlemen of today
only listen to the words of scholars and high officials.
As for the words of the true gentlemen,
they are rare.
Alas!
I speak of the royal words that, without leaving the door or window, transform the world."
*Zēngzǐ* rose,
descended from his mat, and replied,
"May I venture to ask what are the royal words?"
*Kǒngzǐ* did not answer.
*Zēngzǐ* said,
"It is difficult to attend the Master at leisure,
therefore I dare to ask."
*Kǒngzǐ* still did not answer.
*Zēngzǐ* became respectful and fearful,
hitched up his robe and withdrew,
stood with his mat on his back.
After a while,
*Kǒngzǐ* sighed,
turned and said to *Zēngzǐ*,
"Shēn!
You can be told the Way of the enlightened king."
Zēngzǐ said:
"I dare not consider myself sufficient,
but I would like to learn from what I have heard."
The Master said:
"Sit down,
I will tell you.
The Way,
is how to illuminate virtue;
virtue,
is how to venerate the Way.
Therefore, without virtue the Way is not venerated,
without the Way, virtue is not illuminated.
Even if one has fine horses of the state,
if they are not trained and ridden according to the proper way,
one cannot travel far;
even if one has vast lands and many people,
if they are not governed according to the proper way,
one cannot achieve hegemony.
Therefore,
in the past, the enlightened kings cultivated the Seven Teachings internally,
and practiced the Three Attainments externally.
When the Seven Teachings are cultivated,
then one can defend;
when the Three Attainments are practiced,
then one can conquer.
The way of the enlightened king,
in his defense,
surely deflects attacks from a thousand miles away;
in his conquests,
surely returns the army as if from resting on a mat.
Therefore it is said,
"Cultivate internally the seven teachings,
and the ruler above will not be weary;
enact externally the three reaches,
and wealth will not be wasted."
This is called the way of the enlightened king."
Zēngzǐ said:
"An enlightened king who is neither wearying nor wasteful,
may I be permitted to hear about it?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"In the past,
Emperor Shùn had Yǔ on his left and Gāo Yáo on his right,
and without leaving his mat, the world was governed.
If it is like this,
how could the ruler above be weary?
If the governance is not centered,
it is the ruler's misfortune;
if the orders are not carried out,
it is the ministers' fault.
If the tax is only one-eleventh,
and the people's labor is used
for no more than three days a year;
and when entering the mountains and marshes, it is done in the proper season without levies;
and tolls at the passes, inspections at the markets, and shops in the city do not collect taxes.
These are the ways to generate wealth,
and the enlightened king economizes on these,
how then is wealth wasted?"
Zēngzǐ said:
"May I venture to ask what are the seven teachings?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"If superiors respect the elderly,
then inferiors will be more filial;
if superiors honor age,
then inferiors will be more fraternal;
if superiors enjoy giving,
then inferiors will be more generous;
if superiors are close to the virtuous,
then inferiors will choose their friends wisely;
if superiors love virtue,
then inferiors will not conceal anything;
if superiors despise greed,
then inferiors will be ashamed to contend;
if superiors are upright and yield,
then inferiors will be ashamed to hoard.
These are called the Seven Teachings.
The Seven Teachings
are the foundation of governing the people.
When the teachings and governance are established,
then the foundation is upright.
All superiors
are examples for the people.
If the standard is upright, what will not be upright?
Therefore, a ruler should first establish benevolence within himself;
then the high officials will be loyal, and the scholars will be trustworthy,
the people will be honest and the customs simple,
men will be sincere and women chaste.
These six things are the result of instruction.
Spread them throughout the world and in every direction, and they will not be wanting;
apply them in ordinary homes, and they will not be obstructed.
Regulate them with ritual,
establish them with righteousness,
and implement them with obedience,
then the people's rejection of evil will be like pouring hot water on snow!"
Zēngzǐ said:
"The Way has reached its limit;
your disciple is not sufficient to make it clear."
Confucius said:
"Shēn, do you think that is all?
There is more.
In the past,
the enlightened kings had methods for governing the people;
they would certainly divide the land and enfeoff them,
and distribute responsibilities to govern them;
then virtuous people would have nowhere to hide,
and violent people would have nowhere to lie low.
They would order the officials to examine and evaluate them daily and periodically,
to promote and employ the virtuous and good,
and to demote and dismiss the unworthy.
If that is the case, then the worthy will be pleased, and the unworthy will be afraid,
Have compassion for widowers and widows,
provide for orphans and the childless,
relieve the poor,
encourage filial piety and brotherly love,
select the talented;
if these seven are cultivated,
then within the four seas there will be no criminals.
The ruler's affection for the people below
is like that of the hands and feet for the heart;
the people's affection for the ruler above
is like that of a young child for its loving mother.
When those above and those below are so affectionate towards each other,
then orders are followed,
commands are carried out,
the people cherish his virtue,
those near are pleased and submit,
those far away come and attach themselves;
this is the achievement of governance.
Now, by spreading the fingers, one knows the *cun* (inch);
by spreading the hand, one knows the *chi* (foot);
by extending the elbow, one knows the *xun* (fathom);
these are the principles of not being far off.
The Zhōu Dynasty system was such that,
three hundred paces made a *li* (里, approximately 0.5 km),
a thousand paces formed a *jing* (井, a unit of land division),
three *jing* made a *lie* (埒, an enclosure),
three *lie* made a *ju* (矩, a square),
fifty *li* made a *du* (都, a capital city),
To enfeoff a hundred li to establish a state;
is to accumulate stores and gather resources there.
To be concerned with whether travelers have what they need.
Therefore, the Mányí barbarians and all the Xià peoples,
although their clothing and headwear are different,
and their languages do not match,
none fail to come as guests.
Therefore it is said:
Without a market, the people are not lacking;
without punishments, the people are not disordered.
Hunting and fishing with nets,
is not to fill palaces and chambers;
levying taxes from the common people,
is not to fill treasuries and storehouses.
To feel compassion and distress to make up for deficiencies,
and use ritual restraint to lessen excess.
Believing in much and using few appearances,
such rituals can be upheld,
such words can be repeated,
such traces can be followed;
like eating when hungry,
like drinking when thirsty,
the people trust them,
like the inevitable verification of cold and heat.
Therefore, seeing the distant as near,
is not because the way is near,
but because of seeing bright virtue.
Therefore, weapons of war do not move, yet there is awe;
To employ benefits without bestowing them, yet be close to the people,
this is what is meant by the "guarding" of an enlightened ruler,
he who repels attacks from a thousand *lǐ* away."
Zēngzǐ said:
"May I venture to ask, what are the 'Three Perfections'?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Perfect propriety requires no concession, and the world is well-ordered;
Perfect reward requires no expenditure, and the scholars of the world are pleased;
Perfect music makes no sound, and the people of the world are harmonious.
An enlightened ruler diligently practices these Three Perfections,
therefore the rulers of the world can be known,
the scholars of the world can be made his subjects,
and the people of the world can be employed."
Zēngzǐ said:
"May I venture to ask, what is the meaning of this principle?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"In ancient times, the enlightened rulers
were sure to know all the names of the good scholars in the world;
having known their names,
they also knew their substance,
and also knew their number and where they were located.
Then, based on the ranks of the world, they honored them;
this is what is meant by 'Perfect propriety requires no concession, and the world is well-ordered.'
Based on the emoluments of the world, they enriched the scholars of the world;
this is what is meant by 'Perfect reward requires no expenditure, and the scholars of the world are pleased.'
If it is like this,
then the reputation of the world will rise up,
this is what is meant by 'Perfect music makes no sound, and the people of the world are harmonious.'
故曰：
所謂天下之至仁者，
能合天下之至親也；
所謂天下之至明者，

能舉天下之至賢者也。 Therefore it is said: Those who are called the most benevolent in the world are able to unite those who are the most closely related in the world; those who are called the most discerning in the world are able to elevate those who are the most virtuous in the world.
此三者咸通，
然後可以征。 When these three things are all accomplished, then one can undertake a campaign.
是故仁者莫大乎愛人，
智者莫大乎知賢，

賢政者莫大乎官能。 Therefore, for the benevolent, nothing is greater than loving the people; for the wise, nothing is greater than knowing the virtuous; for virtuous governance, nothing is greater than employing the capable.
有土之君，
修此三者，
則四海之內，
共命而已矣。 A ruler who possesses territory, if he cultivates these three things, then within the four seas, (people) will only obey his commands.
夫明王之所征，
必道之所廢者也。 The campaigns of an enlightened king are necessarily directed towards those who have abandoned the Way.
是故誅其君而改其政，
弔其民而不奪其財。 Therefore, (he) punishes their ruler and reforms their government, consoles their people and does not seize their wealth.
故明王之政，
猶時雨之降，
降至則民說矣。 Therefore, the government of an enlightened king is like timely rain that descends; when it descends, the people are pleased.
是故行施彌博，
得親彌眾，

此之謂還師衽席之上。 」 Therefore, his acts of generosity are exceedingly extensive, and the number of those who become close to him is exceedingly numerous. This is what is meant by "returning the army on a mat and pillow."
大昏解第四 Chapter Four: Explanation of the Great Wedding
Kǒngzǐ shì zuò yú Āi Gōng. Kǒngzǐ was attending Āi Gōng (Duke Ai).
公曰：
「Gǎn wèn rén dào shú wèi dà? 」 "May I ask, in the way of humanity, what is the greatest?"
Kǒngzǐ qiǎo rán zuò sè ér duì yuē: Kǒngzǐ looked grave and replied:
「Jūn zhī jí cǐ yán yě, "That you, O lord, have raised this question,
bǎixìng zhī huì yě, is a blessing for the common people.
gù chén gǎn wú cí ér duì? Therefore, how could your subject dare not to answer?
Rén dào zhèng wèi dà. In the way of humanity, governance is the greatest.
Fú zhèng zhě, zhèng yě. Now, governance is rectification.
Jūn wèi zhèng, If the ruler is upright,
zé bǎixìng cóng ér zhèng yǐ. then the common people will follow and be upright.
Jūn zhī suǒ wèi, What the ruler does,
bǎixìng zhī suǒ cóng; is what the common people follow;
jūn bù wéi zhèng, if the ruler is not upright,
bǎixìng hé suǒ cóng hū? 」 what will the common people follow?"
Gōng yuē: The Duke said:
「Gǎn wèn wéi zhèng rú zhī hé? 」 "May I ask, what should governance be like?"
Kǒngzǐ duì yuē: Kǒngzǐ replied:
「Fūfù bié, "Husband and wife have their separate roles,
nánnǚ qīn, men and women are affectionate,
jūn chén xìn; ruler and subject are trustworthy;
sān zhě zhèng, If these three are rectified,
zé shù wù cóng zhī. 」 then all things will follow."
Gōng yuē: The Duke said:
「Guǎrén suī wú néng yě, "Although I, the寡人 (term used by dukes/kings to refer to themselves), am incompetent,
yuàn rú suǒyǐ xíng sān zhě zhī dào, I wish to know the way to implement these three,
kě dé wén hū? 」 may I be allowed to hear it?"
Kǒngzǐ duì yuē: Kǒngzǐ replied:
「Gǔ zhī wéi zhèng, "In ancient times, governance,
Loving people is paramount;
therefore, in governing the love of people,
ritual is paramount;
therefore, in governing ritual,
respect is paramount;
the utmost of respect
the great marriage is paramount;
the great marriage has arrived;
the great marriage having arrived,
wearing the crown and personally welcoming [the bride];
the personal welcoming [of the bride],
is respect.
Therefore, the gentleman cultivates respect as a means of being close to his relatives;
abandoning respect,
is to abandon one's relatives;
not being close nor respectful,
is not showing honor.
Love and respect,
are they not the foundation of governance?"
The Duke said:

do not utter words of instruction and correction,
do not choose worthy people to entrust themselves to,

they see the small and are blind to the great,

they follow things like a stream,

The Duke said:
"What is meant by shìrén (士人, scholar-official)?"
Kǒngzǐ (孔子) said:
"Those who are called shìrén (士人)
have something settled in their hearts,
and have something to which their plans adhere.
Although they may not be able to exhaust the foundation of the Way and techniques,
they must have something they follow.
Although they may not be able to possess the beauty of a hundred virtues,
they must have a place where they reside [or something they abide by].

but they must carefully examine what they know.
In speech, they do not strive for much,
but they must carefully examine what they say.
In action, they do not strive for much,
but must carefully examine the path they take.
Once knowledge is known,
once words are spoken,
once actions are taken,
then it is like the form and body of life that cannot be changed;
wealth and honor are not enough to increase it,
poverty and lowliness are not enough to diminish it,
this is a shì rén (士人, scholar). "

"What is called a Jūnzǐ (君子, gentleman)?"

"What is called a Jūnzǐ (君子, gentleman) is one whose

his thoughts and considerations are clear and bright,
and his words are not dogmatic;
